key_insight: LottieGPT converts vector animation primitives into discrete tokens so an autoregressive model can generate, edit, and conditionally synthesize resolution-independent vector animations the way language models generate text.
problem_solved: Existing generative models operate in raster space and cannot produce compact, editable, resolution-independent vector animations (e.g., Lottie/SVG), limiting web and UI animation synthesis and downstream editing.
method: Design a tokenization scheme that encodes vector primitives (paths, fills, strokes), parametric transforms, keyframe timing, and easing into a sequential token vocabulary.
Train an autoregressive transformer to model token sequences, enabling unconditional and conditioned generation (text/sketch/timeline) of vector animation sequences.
Decode generated tokens back to vector formats (e.g., Lottie/SVG) with loss-aware reconstruction and support for semantic editing and interpolation.
impact: Enables compact, editable, and high-fidelity animation generation that integrates into web/UI pipelines and creative tools, reducing asset sizes and enabling controllable animation synthesis for ML-driven design workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: vector primitives → tokenization → autoregressive transformer → vector decoder (Lottie/SVG)
Before/after comparison: raster GIF/video vs. generated vector animation showing resolution independence and file-size difference
Sequence visualization: token timeline aligned with rendered keyframes and easing curves
Use-case mockups: web UI editor generating and editing animations from text or sketch inputs
paper_title: LottieGPT: Tokenizing Vector Animation for Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Junhao Chen, Kejun Gao, Yuehan Cui, Mingze Sun, Mingjin Chen
